QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_31

question.text: For domestic-violence resolution under SAS-400, the MOST suitable OUTCOME indicator to audit is:

answer.text: Number of helpline calls received (this is demand / activity)
Number of DV cases legally resolved / referred to One-Stop Centres + victim's self-reported safety-perception score 6 months post-intervention

explanation.text: **The Logic:** DV resolution outcome is multi-dimensional: legal resolution (objective), victim safety-perception score (subjective but crucial). Both should be audited together, 6 months post-intervention to test sustainability. **The Trap:** Options A and C are activity/output counts — they say nothing about resolution. Option D is PR material. **Cross-Exam Context:** Outcome-measurement structure common to X-A / X-B (Investment Adviser impact) and V-B (MF Foundation). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Always build a safety-perception scale into the DV programme baseline — without it, 'DV reduced' is an unauditable narrative.
